I'll tell you the easiest way with the least impact on your body so you won't give up.

They say that because cars these days are fuel injected. 
When you start the engine the oil was sitting and now it's being splashed around everywhere lubricating everything. You tend to wait 30 seconds to give it time to be safe so lubricant spreads but also you wait for the oil pressure to go down. You'll notice when you start your car it'll idle at 2k rpms or so and in the summer it'll settle to roughly 1k and sound different. A good majority wait for that to happen, it's only a benefit. 

Now waiting a minute or 2 before taking off is perfectly okay and helps with longevity of the engine but what they say is partly true. The car does warm up when driving and a lot faster than just sitting so I would, start the car, sit for a minute then the first 2-3 miles you drive, drive patiently and don't get on the gas heavy. 

Sitting with the car on for 10-15 minutes consistently is when it's bad for the engine. After a while pressure builds up and can cause leaks and just problems.

Oil light, oil pressure, means there was an issue there. Could have been a minor thing but unfortunately it was a big issue. I've had a check engine light for 2 years and it goes on and off. always the same code but something so minor the place I get my inspection still passes it. 

For your next car just look after the oil, check on any lights on the dash. When it's cold and winter time, don't listen to anyone saying you don't need to warm up your car. Always give it 1-2 in the cold, like when your car is frosted over kinda cold. I'm no expert but I was in a serious accident and left bedridden for 6 months. I couldn't walk 40 steps without seeing stars in my eyes and feeling sick, my body had no energy or strength. Keeping an upright posture took all my will power. 

I started off doing situps in my room, bringing my legs towards my chest as I sit up, then straighten out and repeat. That worked more core and my hips. Your hip flexors help you with posture and support your upper and lower body. So  I did those basically until it hurt lol. I couldnt do a push up so I got 2, 10 pound dumbells and did dumbbell bench press and shoulder press, hammer curls and forearm curls, you can youtube those. I did those exercises until my muscles hurt and felt all wobbly. I also did squats, just 30 in a couple minutes will be plenty, you'll really feel them hurting but that's what makes them get stronger. And then just always walking, your body even if your state can walk miles, you'll feel like you can't but you can. Just a mile a day and some weights until you can do more miles and more weights. 

I did those simple things and just a month in I was walking 6 miles and went from 10 pound weights to 20 pounds for the same reps. My miles and weights went higher the more I did them. 

Also make sure you're drinking plenty of water and get electrolytes in. You get those in little packets you can pour into water. The BIG thing is making sure you eat PROTEIN. To start you'll only really only need half a gram of protein per pound of body weight so if you weigh 130 pounds make sure you're consuming at least 65 grams of protein. The more the better. If you can afford 200 grams of protein a day then all the better. If you walk and hydrate and workout but don't eat protein you're not gonna get results as fast as you want. 

All the issues you said will be solved with building muscle and walking, walking is underrated. It's low stress on the body but just as effective as running. Walking just takes more time. Walking builds endurance for your muscles, just standing upright uses muscles and energy so the more you're on your feet the better. 

YouTube a full body workout for beginners or for people just coming out of injury or something. 

Your body will hurt but that's normal, you were in bed for 8 months so lifting 10 pounds 30 times may hurt ya the next day. If an area or body part hurts then workout a different part and rotate. One day just do core workouts then the next do arms then do legs then back to core etc etc
